subject: Clarify billing for multi-file ingest and request for temporary smoothing credit
messages:
From: Emma Liu <procurement@novamed.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Jan 2028 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify billing for multi-file ingest and temporary smoothing credit

Hi Jonas,

Hope you’re well. We received the January invoice (attached: sample-invoice.pdf) and noticed a ~35% delta compared to our expected estimate for the month. The bulk of our calls in the period were file-ingest requests where we POST batches of PDF reports (10–40 pages each). Two things I need clarified:

1) How are tokens accounted for when we upload multi-page PDFs that are OCR'd and chunked server-side? Do attachments map to a single request token count or do you count per chunk after splitting?
2) We see per-call rounding up at the invoice line item level — is there a minimum quantum per request that would explain the uplift?

We can share the telemetry CSV if it helps. For now, given the unexpected charge and since this is an ongoing pilot, would Redwood consider a provisional smoothing credit while you investigate? Something in the $400–$600 range would keep us within budget for January and give us time to align model/ingest settings.

Attached: sample-invoice.pdf (invoice lines highlighted)

Thanks,
Emma Liu
Procurement 
NovaMed

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: Emma Liu <procurement@novamed.com>
Cc: camila.reyes@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Jan 2028 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify billing for multi-file ingest and temporary smoothing credit

Hi Emma — thanks for the note and for attaching the invoice. Quick answers up front, then next steps:

- Short answer on counting: Redwood measures tokens after content is normalized (OCR -> text) and tokenized by the model's tokenizer. For multi-file POSTs we treat each API call independently; internal chunking only affects how the request is processed, but token accounting is total input tokens produced by the tokenizer for the request.
- Rounding/minimums: your account is on the default per-call quantum of 1,000 input-token units for metering (we round up to the nearest 1k by default for small, bursty requests). That explains why lots of small file uploads can create an above-expected step function on the invoice.

I’ve looped in Camila (AE) and Ben (Finance) to review whether a temporary smoothing credit is reasonable and to validate the invoice mapping. Can you send the telemetry CSV and one raw sample PDF/text extract (tokenization-sample.txt) so we can reproduce the token counts locally? Also sharing the HubSpot deal link would be helpful.

Proposed immediate action: I can provisionally approve a $500 credit while we reconcile, subject to finance sign-off. If that works, I’ll confirm later today.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Sales
Redwood Inference

Camila / Ben — forwarding Emma's note + invoice. Key facts I pulled while triaging:

- The customer is sending many small PDFs (average 18 pages) which our ingest path OCRs and then chunks into ~800–3,200-token pieces depending on segmentation settings.
- Metering picks up the total tokenized length per API call and then applies the per-call quantum (1k input-token rounding up) before summing for the invoice period. In practice, 6 small files in separate requests -> 6 * roundup( token_count / 1k ) units.

Questions for finance:
1) If we issue a $500 provisional credit, should it be recorded as a one-time invoice credit or as a promo that offsets future monthly usage?
2) If we change their per-call quantum to 200 input tokens (pilot-friendly), is there a way to set that as an account-level metering override for February while we advise on batching/merge recommendations? That would materially reduce the rounding noise but affects how we account for pilot customers.

Proposed reconciliation approach:
- Reproduce tokenization on a sample PDF (I attached tokenization-sample.txt and sample-telemetry.csv).
- Map each invoice line to the request IDs in the telemetry and show the rounding delta per request.
- Issue $500 provisional credit applied to invoice JAN-2028 if finance agrees.

Ben — can you confirm process/cashflow impact and whether a temporary per-account quantum override is allowed?

Thanks,
Jonas

From: camila.reyes@redwood.com
To: Emma Liu <procurement@novamed.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 15 Jan 2028 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify billing for multi-file ingest and request for temporary smoothing credit

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear reproduction artifacts. We dug into your telemetry and reproduced the tokenization on a local run. Short summary and concrete next steps below.

Executive summary:
- Root cause: your ingest flow sends many separate PDF upload requests. Each request is OCR'd -> tokenized; Redwood then applies the account's per-call metering quantum (1,000 input-token rounding) which amplified small requests. The tokenizer output matched your sample: individual requests were frequently in the 200–800 token range, which the 1k quantum rounded up to 1k per request.
- What we changed: we applied a one-time $500 invoice credit to your JAN-2028 invoice (line: JAN-28-NOVAMED) — you should see this reflected in the portal and in the revised PDF (linked). We also enabled a temporary pilot metering override that reduces per-call quantum to 200 input-token units for your account for the month of February to reduce rounding noise while you test batching patterns.

Action items / recommended changes on your side:
- Combine multiple small PDFs into a single multi-file request when possible (this will consolidate token accounting into a single request and avoid repeated rounding).
- If you must submit separate files, consider client-side batching (send up to N files in a single multipart call).
- Review ingestion segmentation: switching to ‘paragraph’ segmentation reduces artificial chunks.

Attachments / links:
- Revised-invoice-JAN-2028.pdf (live in the billing portal)
- Reproduction notes and request-id mapping: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-novamed-billing
- HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.redwood.com/deal/NOVA-2028-SMB-07

Follow-up: Jonas / I will schedule a 30-minute walkthrough next week to go over API examples and batching patterns if you'd like.

Best,
